correctness.rationale: For g(t)=exp(-at)-exp(-bt), unique single-source t0=log(b/a)/(b-a). At t>s the derivative is a difference of two exponentials with at most one zero; right derivative at s is (b-a)(k-kappa(s)), kappa(s)=(a exp(-as)-b exp(-bs))/(b-a). Thus exactly two strict maxima iff s>t0 and k>kappa(s), with equality no second peak. Derivative of kappa changes sign only at 2t0, giving reentrant separation windows, max kappa_*=(a/b)^((a+b)/(b-a)), fold inverse-root behavior and universal kappa_*<exp(-2). Independently checked exact rational witness for (a,b,k)=(1,2,1/16): at s=log(9/4),log4,log16 the post-outfall derivative signs 17/1296,-1/16,1/128 yield 2,1,2. This proof is analytic, not an inference from finite checks.
